liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **St Stephen** (6 reviews): Reviewer says this was the first Stephen since 1-10-79; Reviewer says audience tapes of Stephen give goosebumps; a man left his wheelchair, danced the whole song, then cried [34][35][37][40][42][43]
- **Keep Your Day Job** (2 reviews): Garcia stays right on the melody, builds tension on key notes, then swoops into the chord changes with a bend; The song was still new, so Garcia takes only one solo pass; his fills are also praised [33][40]
- **Wang Dang Doodle** (1 review): Jerry began in the wrong key, and Bobby and Phil audibly reacted; Bobby's verse sounded off; The band recovered after the shaky start [44]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): Reviewer rates the jam as among the best of the early arrangements [38]

## Setlist highlights

- **St Stephen**: back after 378 archived shows (1735 days) [45]

## The recordings

- **gd83-10-11.silberman.gustin.344.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 185 min; rated 4.56/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Highest-quality audience recording, placing the listener back in the crowd [41]
- **gd1983-10-11.143258.senn421-beyer-m201.holbrook.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 142 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1983-10-11.sbd.harrell.14525.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [5]
- **gd1983-10-11.143259.senn421-beyer-m201.holbrook.flac2448**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 142 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]. Said about its sound: Volume fluctuates from about 2:35 to a tune's end, with mic pre-amp distortion before levels drop [6]
- **gd83-10-11.sbd.harrell.7339.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 140 min; rated 4/5 by 40 [9]. Said about its sound: On the soundboard, audience reaction to Stephen is barely audible; Soundboard is only so-so, not crisp [42][43]

## Around the show

- Reviewer heard from Jerry's dealer in Richmond at the Hyatt that the band rehearsed Revolution, played the second MSG night [34]
- The year before, reviewer saw the band getting into a limo in NYC, shouted for St. Stephen, and Bill gave a thumbs up [37]
- Many fans knew the band had sound checked Stephen, yet the crowd response was still huge [38]
- The Dead scene was not yet huge, so the crowd was very experienced [41]
- Reviewer found Jerry's voice poor and several song transitions rocky or sloppy [43]
- Bobby told the crowd Jerry's speaker had blown out, so they were changing it [6]
- Garcia described Madison Square Garden as juiced, with an energy unlike any other venue the Dead played [46]
- Source credits Dan Healy and the venue for the cassette sounding so good [48]
- Reviewer, who was there, finds the first set nearly better than the second [40]
- Reviewer ranks a few 1983 shows, this among them, as the strongest of the decade despite Garcia's habit [41]

- **gd83-10-11.silberman.gustin.344.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jeff Silberman; source: Audience: Sennheiser 441's [1]. Also: Recorded by Holbrook using Sennheiser 421 and Beyer M201 microphones [3]
